name: Nick Bostrom

summary.text: Nick Bostrom is a philosopher who founded the Future of Humanity Institute (FHI) at the University of Oxford in 2005 and directed it until Oxford's Faculty of Philosophy closed it on April 16, 2024, after which he resigned from the university and founded the non-profit Macrostrategy Research Initiative. He is the author of Superintelligence (2014) and of 'Transhumanist Values', which argues that human nature should be improved through technology. In January 2023 he published an apology for a 1996 email to the Extropians mailing list that contained a racial slur; Oxford opened an investigation, and he has said the university later told him it did not consider him a racist.

facts.claim: The Future of Humanity Institute, an interdisciplinary research group at the University of Oxford founded by Bostrom in 2005, was closed by the Faculty of Philosophy on April 16, 2024 after 19 years. Bostrom was its director for its entire existence. The institute's final report said the faculty had frozen fundraising and hiring in 2020 and decided in late 2023 not to renew staff contracts.
facts.quote: The Faculty of Philosophy imposed a freeze on fundraising and hiring in 2020, and decided not to renew the contracts of staff in late 2023, according to the Institute's final report published on April 12th.

facts.claim: In a statement emailed to The Guardian after the closure, Bostrom described pressure to conform and a 'death by bureaucracy'. Oxford's spokesperson said the university had taken the difficult decision to close the institute and thanked its researchers.
facts.quote: In an emailed statement to The Guardian, he described a pressure to conform and a death by bureaucracy.

facts.quote: The institute's largest team, the Governance of AI Program, became an independent organisation after spinning out of the university in 2021.

facts.claim: On January 9, 2023 Bostrom published 'Apology for an Old Email' on his website, concerning a 1996 message he had sent to the Extropians mailing list while a student in London that contained a racial slur. He wrote that he had apologised at the time and apologised 'again unreservedly', and that the email 'does not accurately represent my views, then or now'. He said he published it after learning that a critic was likely to make the email public.
facts.quote: I apologized for writing it at the time, within 24 hours; and I apologize again unreservedly today.

facts.claim: After the email became public in January 2023, the University of Oxford said it and the Faculty of Philosophy were investigating the matter and condemned the views expressed. According to an excerpt from Tom Ough's book The Anti-Catastrophe League, the university wrote to Bostrom in August 2023 that it did not consider him a racist or that he held racist views and regarded his apology as sincere.
facts.quote: In August 2023, the university told him "we do not consider you to be a racist or that you hold racist views," and said it considered his apology sincere.

facts.claim: In 'Transhumanist Values' Bostrom defines transhumanism as a loosely defined movement developed over the preceding two decades and lists among its aims the radical extension of human health-span, eradication of disease, elimination of unnecessary suffering and augmentation of human intellectual, physical and emotional capacities. The paper appeared in the Journal of Philosophical Research, vol. 30, 2005, with earlier versions dating from 2001 and 2003.

facts.claim: After Oxford closed FHI in April 2024, Bostrom resigned from the university and continued his research as founder and principal researcher of the non-profit Macrostrategy Research Initiative.
facts.quote: After Oxford closed FHI in April 2024, Bostrom resigned from the university and continued his research as founder and Principal Researcher of the nonprofit Macrostrategy Research Initiative.

openQuestions: Several outlets describe FHI as 'Elon Musk-funded'; the amount, date and route of any Musk donation were not established and no connection to elon-musk was recorded.

Bostrom's co-founding of the World Transhumanist Association (now Humanity+) with David Pearce in 1998 appeared only in Wikipedia-derived material and was not recorded; a Humanity+ or Bostrom page would source it.
Robin Hanson is described as a research associate of FHI in Wikipedia-derived material; not recorded for lack of a primary source.
The August 2023 university letter is quoted through a book excerpt hosted on Bostrom's own site; Oxford has not been found to have published the investigation's outcome.
